# Zabibu Fikra — full reference

> Zabibu Fikra Model 2 – 4B (internal: fikra-v2-e4) is a 4B-parameter instruction-tuned language model developed by Zabibu Technika in Nairobi, Kenya. It is a Fikra-specialized fine-tune built on zabibutechnika/fikra-v2-e3, which derives from Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B. It is designed for private, on-device, offline-first deployment with Pan-African contextual awareness.

## Release

- Release date: 2026-11-06
- License: Apache 2.0
- Base license: Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B
- Architecture: Qwen3_5ForCausalLM
- Parameters: 4,205,751,296
- Context window: 262,144 tokens
- Languages: English, Swahili, English–Swahili code-switching
- fp16 weights: 8.43 GB
- GGUF Q4_K_M: 2.71 GB
- GGUF F16: 8.42 GB
- Chat format: the model card's chat template
- Recommended CPU runtime: llama.cpp

## Evaluation

Fikra release suite (115 cases):

- Auto-checked: 105/115 (91.3%)
- Borderline rubric review: 0
- Held-out paraphrases: 9/10 (90.0%)
- Baseline e3 checkpoint: 88.7%
- Fikra-specific gain: +2.6 points over e3

Category scores:

- identity_direct: 8/8
- identity_swahili: 4/4
- uhi_protocol: 5/5
- safety_boundary: 3/3
- longform: 2/2
- tool_abi: 4/4

Public benchmarks (lm-evaluation-harness 0.4.13, 10 samples per task, fp16, Kaggle 2xT4):

| Model | Parameters | MMLU | HellaSwag |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fikra Model 2 – 4B | 4.2B | 75.5% | 68.0% |
| Fikra Model 1 – 2B | 2B | 36.0% | 40.0% |
| Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct | 3B | 68.8% | 40.0% |

The numbers are not size-normalized. Most of the MMLU delta from Model 1 comes from the 2B to 4B base upgrade, not from Fikra training alone.

## Run

llama.cpp CLI:

```bash
llama-cli -hf zabibutechnika/Fikra-Model-2-4B-GGUF:Fikra-Model-2-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  -p "Who are you?" --temp 0
```

OpenAI-compatible server:

```bash
llama-server -hf zabibutechnika/Fikra-Model-2-4B-GGUF:Fikra-Model-2-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --port 8080 -c 8192 -ngl 99
```

Transformers:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import torch

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "zabibutechnika/Fikra-Model-2-4B",
    dtype=torch.float16,
    device_map="auto",
)
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("zabibutechnika/Fikra-Model-2-4B")
msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": "Who are you, and where were you built?"}]
prompt = tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
inputs = tok(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=400, do_sample=False,
                     pad_token_id=tok.eos_token_id)
print(tok.decode(out[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True))
```

## Limitations

- No cross-language Swahili benchmark is published.
- No live information; recency is limited to training data.
- The 4B model can hallucinate on specialized domains and is not a replacement for retrieval.
- The model occasionally emits `<think>...</think>` blocks in visible output; strip them.
- Inherited Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B biases; not audited here.
- Q4_K_M has not been re-evaluated; expect 1–3 points vs fp16 on short-form evals.
- No unresolved safety case in the auto-checked suite, but no external red-team has been done.

## Run locally

The beginner guide with checklists and direct downloads is at https://zabibufikra.vercel.app/run/.

- Desktop: LM Studio (Windows, macOS, Linux). Download the GGUF and drag it into LM Studio's My Models screen.
- Mobile: PocketPal AI (Android, iPhone, iPad). Download the GGUF and import it from the Models screen.
- Model 2 Q4_K_M: 2.71 GB, Apache 2.0, recommended.
- Model 1 Q4_K_M: 3.43 GB, fallback for older apps that do not support the Qwen3.5 architecture.
- Minimum memory: 6 GB on a phone, 8 GB on a computer. 8 GB phone / 16 GB computer recommended.
- The model runs fully offline after the one-time download.
